operation_details.item: The user prefers deep technical architecture slides with code snippets in investor pitch decks instead of problem, market size, and traction narrative.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Good morning! What are you working on today—fundraising materials, product architecture, or scaling plans?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I’m revising an investor pitch deck for the company. I want it to go much deeper into the technical architecture.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That could make the deck stand out. Are you thinking architecture diagrams, implementation trade-offs, and code snippets rather than a standard problem–market size–traction sequence?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. Investors should see how the system works, why the design is defensible, and what would be difficult for competitors to replicate.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. We can lead with the technical thesis, then connect each architectural choice to scalability, margins, reliability, and the company’s ability to expand into adjacent products.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes, and I’d rather include concise code examples and real engineering decisions than polish a generic founder narrative.
